title: pstack checkpoint: shared mutable state and conflict policy
description:
Document the conflict policy before implementation. The design should make accidental same-file concurrent writes hard to express. The BFF should own active Office sessions and conflict checks. The host should enforce expected revision or idempotency on writes.

## Required Skills
pstack-playbooks,principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state
design:
This bead is the Feature playbook throughput checkpoint item for shared mutable state.

Shared state includes vault file bytes, document revisions, active Office sessions, callback status, pane state, and agent write targets. The default policy is separation before serialization. Agents write checkpoints or staged copies when a human owns an active dirty editor session.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Shared mutable state is enumerated.
[ ] Human edit sessions, Document Server cache keys, agent writes, and vault revisions have an ownership rule.
[ ] Dirty human edits block agent overwrite or force a staged-copy path.
[ ] Document keys include tenant, path, and content revision so cache collisions are impossible.

title: Host playbook + tools: mailbox, channel invite, cron, workflow (not raw API dump)
description:
## Wanted product

Every agent turn gets a **short host playbook** plus **real tools** so they know how to: message another agent, manage channel membership, create a scheduled task (cron), create a workflow. Same idea as "ask them to create a job."

## What this is not

Do **not** inject a dump of Portal HTTP routes and tell the model to fetch them. That is how we got fake "I messaged X" icons, no target inbound, and recursive loops.

The inbound spine **is** the request log. Agents never POST /api/chat/... as Jack. Each capability is a **tool**; the host implements it as enqueueInbound / existing BFF create routes.

Do **not** give a writable "stream of all communications." Jack SSE is a view. A2A is mailbox.send then a work item on the target thread (D8).

## Tools (host-owned)

| Tool | Does |
| --- | --- |
| mailbox.send | origin notice + target enqueue source=mailbox |
| channel.add_member | roster grow (lp-k5c4.20) |
| scheduled_task.create | existing POST /api/settings/crons path, as owner |
| workflow.create | existing workflow create path, as owner |

Playbook in the turn system_prompt names **these tools** and when to use them (a page, not an OpenAPI spec). Tool schemas are the contract.

## Recursion

- Fuse: 40/room/hour and ≤8 consecutive a2a without a human (lp-v62i)
- mailbox.send wakes `to` only; never nested startTurn on the caller
- Tools that create jobs/workflows do not immediately re-enter the same turn
- Hop cap / loop_notice stay

## Split

- Platform: playbook text, tool allow-list, BFF handlers, chrome
- lac-r9w: tool runtime on the harness runner (blocks no-tools complete)

## Acceptance

- [ ] Playbook injected on 1:1 and channel turns (not a Settings fixture)
- [ ] All four tools listed above exist and are what the playbook names
- [ ] Jack "message Drift that we're slipping" → mailbox.send, not prose-only
- [ ] Jack "add Drift to #ops" → channel.add_member
- [ ] Jack "every morning ping me the vault index" → scheduled_task.create
- [ ] No agent HTTP client against /api/*
- [ ] Loop test: A mailboxes B mailboxes A stops at cap; no infinite enqueue
acceptance_criteria: Short playbook names mailbox.send, channel.add_member, scheduled_task.create, workflow.create. Host implements them. Model never POSTs /api/*. Jack can ask for message/invite/cron/workflow. A→B→A stops at hop cap. No all-comms writable stream.
close_reason: Done. Branch beads/lp-k5c4-inbound-work-spine-plan 58062dcf. Host playbook HOST_PLAYBOOK injected via host_playbook TurnRequestMetadata on all harness turns (1:1 and group). Tools mailbox.send, channel.add_member, scheduled_task.create, workflow.create as host-owned parsers (no model POST /api/*). Tests wake-policy 19, group-inbound 21, channel-add 17 pass (57 total). Branch pushed.

title: Agent tool channel.add_member so non-members can be invited then @'d
description:
## Symptom

In a channel Jack cannot @ or wake an agent who is not a member. Agents also cannot grow the roster. Product: agents can add other catalog agents to a channel they are in, then message them there.

## Already exists

POST /api/channels/:threadId/members (Jack CSRF + RBAC) and DELETE members with floor-of-two (plan 0016). Agents have no tool. They cannot call Jack's cookie API.

## Design

- New host tool `channel.add_member` { thread_id, agent_id } (or name).
- BFF executes as the owning user, not as a spoofed Portal session.
- After add, the agent is on the roster; @ and mailbox in that room are legal.
- Do not create a new catalog person as a side effect (use existing New agent for that).
- Remove stays Jack UI unless a later bead adds channel.remove_member.
- Fail closed: not a member of the channel → forbidden; unknown agent → not_found; below floor on remove unchanged.

## Do not

- Let the model POST /api/channels/... itself
- Auto-add on @ of a non-member (invite is explicit)
- Recurse: add_member does not start a turn

## Acceptance

- [ ] Tool schema + host handler wraps addChannelMember
- [ ] Agent in #ops can add Drift (catalog, not a member) then @Drift; Drift wakes in #ops
- [ ] Non-member cannot add
- [ ] Playwright: roster grows; @ works; 1:1 of the added agent unchanged
- [ ] Floor of two on human remove still holds
acceptance_criteria: channel.add_member wraps POST members as owner. Agent in-channel can add catalog Drift then @Drift. Fail closed if caller not a member. Playwright roster + wake. No model HTTP. add_member does not start a turn.
close_reason: Done. Branch beads/lp-k5c4.20-channel-add-member 1723fc6b merged f9a2c1. Tool channel.add_member wraps POST members as owner, caller must be member else forbidden, unknown agent not_found, does not auto-add on @, does not start turn. Tests 17 pass.

title: Channel sticky addressee: after @Drift, un-@ follow-ups still wake Drift
description:
## Wanted product

In a channel, after Jack @mentions an agent, the **next human messages with no @ still go to that agent**, the way a group chat keeps talking to the person you just named. Other agents may chime in; they are not auto-woken on every sticky turn.

Today lp-k5c4.15: named @s only; unmentioned → lead. That made `@Drift` stop waking Alpha, but then "ok, also send that file" goes to the lead again.

## Rule

- No @ yet in the channel → lead (unchanged).
- Human @Drift (and not others) → Drift. Sticky addressee = Drift.
- Next human text with no @ → **Drift**, not lead.
- Human @Alpha or @Drift @Beta → sticky set becomes those names.
- Explicit room address (TBD: @channel / @here / talking to the lead by name) clears sticky → lead.
- Persona hops still mailbox.send; do not auto-fan the sticky human turn to the whole roster.
- Fuse + hop cap still bound agent chiming. No recursive wake of the speaker.

## Do not

- Wake the whole roster on sticky turns
- Restore "lead PLUS @s" (lp-k5c4.15 stays)
- Track sticky across 1:1s (1:1 is already that agent)

## Acceptance

- [ ] decideHuman (or a small sticky-addressee layer on the thread) implements the rule above
- [ ] Playwright #testchat: @Drift hi → Drift only; follow-up "what's the status" with no @ → Drift only; Alpha silent
- [ ] @Alpha after that → Alpha, Drift silent
- [ ] Unmentioned first message in a fresh channel still wakes lead
- [ ] Tests in wake-policy; no mention-hop
acceptance_criteria: After human @Drift, next no-@ human turns in that channel wake Drift only. New @ switches. First unmentioned still lead. Playwright #testchat. No roster fan-out. No mention-hop.
close_reason: Done. Branch beads/lp-k5c4.19-sticky-addressee merged to beads/lp-k5c4-inbound-work-spine-plan 2944c7ec. Tests: wake-policy.test.ts 19 pass, group-inbound-stamp.test.ts 21 pass (40 total). Sticky addressee thread-scoped: after @Drift, no-@ wakes Drift; new @ switches; @channel clears to lead; first unmentioned still lead; no roster fan-out.

title: Mailbox icon without target inbound (tools runner + prove Drift 1:1)
description:
## Symptom

Jack tells an agent to message another agent. Origin shows a **message icon** / Messaged @X chrome. The target agent's 1:1 (or channel) does **not** get the inbound. Drift stays empty; Cipher looks done.

Seen on localhost :3153 after lp-k5c4.16 (PR 720). BFF can paint origin notice without a tools-capable runner actually calling mailbox.send, or the hop enqueues and the target turn never lands in history/SSE (same turn-id collision / no-tools complete).

## Why

lp-k5c4.16 wired BFF hop chrome (origin system_notice, target enqueue source=mailbox). Acceptance still required a **tools-capable harness runner**. Local createEnvLiteLlmTurnRunner is **no-tools**. The model emits prose ("I messaged Drift") and the host may show icon chrome; Drift is not woken.

Plan 0019 D8 still holds: A2A = mailbox.send append + enqueue on the **target** thread. Not a second hop brain. Not a prompt that says "POST /api/...".

Cross-repo: lac-r9w owns mailbox.send tool runtime. Platform owns authorize, origin notice, enqueue, prove both rooms.

## Do not

- Give the model raw Portal HTTP routes to fetch
- Nested startTurn on the caller room (recursion / loop we already fused)
- Reopen mention-hop (lp-v62i.3.2 retired)

## Acceptance

- [ ] Tools-capable runner on the local/spine path (not no-tools complete)
- [ ] mailbox.send({to, room, text}) → origin Messaged @X notice AND target 1:1 history has source=mailbox inbound
- [ ] Jack "tell Drift X" / agent mailbox: Drift 1:1 is not empty; Drift can reply without Jack in Drift's composer
- [ ] Playwright: origin notice + target 1:1 bubble; no double-wake
- [ ] Fuse still applies (40/hour, ≤8 consecutive a2a, Halt)

title: Agents cannot mailbox peers (no hop, no Messaged @X, no 1:1 inbound)
description:
## Symptom

Agents do not message each other. They only speak when Jack prompts them, and only in the room Jack is in.

Playwright + history 2026-08-27 on `:3153`:

- Cipher 1:1 (`863d17fa`, renamed Stream QA): Jack sent `@Drift hi` / `@Drift NEED YOUR HELP`. Cipher/Muse Spark **answered in Cipher**. No origin notice, no "Messaged @Drift" bar.
- Drift 1:1 (`097b76fc`): still only the earlier `Reply with pong only.` probe. **No hop inbound.**
- Channel #testchat: Alpha writing `@beta your turn` did **not** start a Beta turn (mention-hop retired, lp-v62i.3.2).

Screenshots: `artifacts/ui/lp-k5c4.13/63-cipher-1to1.png`, `62-drift-1to1.png`.

## Why (not a prompt-only bug)

1. Local Lanyard Agent is `createEnvLiteLlmTurnRunner` — **no tools**. It cannot call `mailbox.send`.
2. BFF `mailbox-hop.ts` exists (`mailboxHopOriginNotice` = `A message has been sent to ${name}.`) but **Send does not call it** from a model tool or from agent `@`.
3. Plan 0019 D8: A2A is mailbox append + enqueue `source=mailbox` on **target** `thread_id`. Not implemented on this spine path.
4. Central inbound queue **is** the request log (`inq_k5c4_13_ui`). Missing piece is enqueueing a second room.

This is not fixed by persona copy. The model can only emit text.

## Wanted product (Jack 2026-08-27)

- Lead (or any in-room persona) can message a peer **without Jack in the loop**.
- Origin room shows a **notice bar**: Messaged @Drift (icon), not a fake "I tagged Drift" assistant bubble.
- Target **1:1** (Jack↔Drift) receives the wake and Drift replies there. Drift can mailbox back to Cipher's room.
- Same inbound spine: `source=mailbox` work item on the **target** thread. Serial per room, parallel across rooms.
- Fuse/Halt from lp-v62i still apply (40/hour, ≤8 consecutive a2a, Halt freezes).

Cross-repo: agent `lac-r9w` owns `mailbox.send` tool runtime. Platform owns hop authorize, origin notice chrome, enqueue.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Tools-capable harness runner (not no-tools complete) on the local/spine path
- [ ] `mailbox.send({to, room, text})` → origin `system_notice` / Messaged @X chrome; target 1:1 enqueued `source=mailbox`
- [ ] Jack `@Drift` in Cipher 1:1: Cipher notice + Drift 1:1 reply; Drift 1:1 is not empty
- [ ] Persona in #testchat can mailbox Drift's 1:1 without Jack's next prompt
- [ ] Agent `@` in prose is mailbox.send (deduped), not mention-hop
- [ ] Playwright: Cipher → notice; Drift 1:1 has inbound; no double-wake from mention-hop
- [ ] Do not invent a second hop brain next to mailbox.send
acceptance_criteria: Tools-capable harness runner. mailbox.send enqueues source=mailbox on target 1:1. Origin shows Messaged @X / system_notice. Drift 1:1 receives Cipher hop. Persona can hop without Jack. No mention-hop double-wake. Playwright Cipher→notice + Drift inbound.
notes: Draft PR https://github.com/LanyardBrain/lanyard-platform/pull/720 — mailbox.send wired on spine Send; origin Messaged @X chrome; target 1:1 source=mailbox. decideHuman untouched. Mention-hop still retired. Not closed (needs UI QA).
close_reason: Done. Squash-merged https://github.com/LanyardBrain/lanyard-platform/pull/720. Spine Send mailbox.send: origin Messaged @X notice, target 1:1 source=mailbox.

title: @mention of a non-lead still wakes the channel lead
description:
## Symptom

On localhost Portal `:3153` (BFF `:4153`, always-spine), Jack `@Drift`s in channel **#testchat**. Drift replies, then **lead Alpha also replies**. Same for `@Beta`.

Live capture 2026-08-27:

- Human: `@Drift whats up`
- Drift: `yo nothing much hbu?`
- Alpha: `Yo, Alpha here — not Drift. What's good?`

Screenshots: `artifacts/ui/lp-k5c4.13/61-channel-at-drift-live.png`, `61-channel-at-drift.png`.

## Current code (intentional, wrong product)

`portal/packages/bff/src/wake-policy.ts` `decideHuman`:

```
// Always wake lead plus @s (unique).
return withTargets([lead, ...mentionsWithoutLead], "mention");
```

## Wanted product

- No `@` → lead only (unchanged).
- Human `@NonLead` (and not the lead) → **only those named personas**. Lead stays silent.
- Human `@Lead` or `@Lead` + others → include lead because they were named.
- Agent prose `@Peer` still does **not** fan out (lp-v62i.3.2 mention-hop retired). That is issue 2 (mailbox.send), not this bead.

## Files

- `wake-policy.ts` `decideHuman` + tests
- `group-inbound-stamp.ts` if stamp tests assume lead+@s
- lp-v62i.3.5 tests that lock lead-plus-@s

## Evidence / QA

localhost `http://127.0.0.1:3153/mocklab` · channel `f8820706` · lead Alpha `e8f98ad8` · Drift `2329f153`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Unmentioned channel send still wakes lead only
- [ ] Human `@Drift` wakes Drift only; Alpha does not get a turn
- [ ] Human `@Alpha @Drift` wakes both
- [ ] Vitest for `decideHuman` + Playwright: one persona bubble for `@Drift`
